content.title: General principles of pharmacotherapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
content.summary: Modulation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) and sympathetic nervous system with ACE inhibitors (ACE-I) or an angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI), beta-blockers, and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRA) improves survival, reduces HF hospitalizations, and reduces symptoms in patients with HFrEF. The recommended foundational triad is an ACE-I/ARNI, a beta-blocker, and an MRA. SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin and empagliflozin) added to ACE-I/ARNI/beta-blocker/MRA reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and worsening HF and are recommended for most patients with HFrEF.
recommended_drugs: ACE inhibitors (ACE-I): e.g., captopril, enalapril, lisinopril, ramipril, trandolapril
content.dosing_table_note: Table 8 provides evidence-based starting and target doses for disease-modifying drugs (ACE-I, ARNI, beta-blockers) in HFrEF.
